Which of the following statements about the Indus civilization is not true?
o: Trade and commerce were in an advanced stage
x: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age Civilization. People of this Age were not familiar with iron. The drainage system was advanced and covered with slabs. The trade and commerce were in an advanced stage. The pieces of evidence of both internal and external trade have been found. Many pieces of evidence of worshipping of Mother Goddess from Indus Valley Civilization have been found.

s: A highly advanced water management system of Harappan times has been unearthed at–
x: From Dholavira, a huge Rock-cut reservoir is found, whose size is about 79 m × 12 m and 7 meters deep, having a huge capacity to store water. People of Dholavira were familiar with the advanced water management system. From the earliest evidence, people used to store water in this reservoir by building dams.

s: Based on findings of excavation of Harappan Civilization, what are not true? (i) For all kinds of constructions, same size of bricks were used. (ii) Mostly all the houses were single storey. (iii)Main roads were on average ten meters in width.
x: In Indus Valley Civilisation both baked and raw bricks were used. Generally the dimensional ratio of burned bricks received from all the Indus towns was 4 : 2 : 1. However ornamental bricks from Kalibangan and curved bricks from Chanhudaro have been found. Hence statement (i) is wrong. Most of the houses built in the Indus Valley Civilisation were built with one storey only, but some houses were also built with two stories as evidence of stairs have been found from some houses. Hence statement (ii) is wrong. The width of roads in Harappan cities was generally 10 meters. Hence statement (iii) is right.

s: Who was the excavator of Lothal?
x: S.R. Rao excavated Lothal in 1954-57. Daya Ram Sahni dug Harappa, A. Ghosh dug Kalibangan and J.P. Joshi dug Surkotada and Dholavira.

s: From where the evidence of rock-cut architecture were found, with reference to Harappa Civilisation?
x: Dholavira has stepwells cut in sandstone, which is the rock-cut architecture of the Harappan civilisation. Kalibangan, Kot Diji and Amri are not known for this.

s: Which one of the following ancient towns is wellknown for its elaborate system of water harvesting and management by building a series of dams and channelizing water into connected reservoirs?
x: Dholavira in Gujarat is well known for its elaborate system of water harvesting and management by building a series of dams and channeling water into connected reservoirs.

x: Lothal is the only place of Indus Valley Civilization from where the pieces of evidence of ports have been found, which is located in the east of the city.

s: The first cereal used by man was :
x: There are mainly eight types of food grains consumed by modern human society, namely barley, wheat, maize, millet, sorghum, mustard, oat and rice. These plants were present in the form of weeds in different areas, which were later grown as seeds by human beings at different places, in different times. Although, barley was the first grain to be cultivated by human beings during 8000 B.C. in western Asian countries located between the northeast Mediterranean Sea and Iran. Later, in the same area, wheat was also cultivated around 8000 B.C.

s: The earliest evidence of animal domestication and agriculture in India has come from
x: Uttar Pradesh has been blessed with a rich cultural heritage since prehistoric times. It is noteworthy that Koldihwa situated in the Belan River valley region of the state, has been considered to be the oldest evidence of paddy cultivation in the world for a long time. Similarly, Lahuradev, which currently presents the oldest evidence of paddy cultivation, is also a part of Sant Kabir Nagar district of Uttar Pradesh. Hence statement (1) is correct. Evidence of the oldest agricultural grains barley and paddy has been found from many excavated sites of Uttar Pradesh, evidence of barley and paddy has been found from Mahagada and evidence of paddy has been found from Koldihwa.

The famous female figurine known as 'Dancing Girl', found at Mohenjo-daro, is made of
x: The Dancing Girl is a small bronze figurine, about four inches tall, and is regarded as one of the earliest known bronze sculptures in the world. The figure depicts a young girl in a confident pose, wearing numerous bangles on her left arm and ornaments on her right. Her posture resembles the later tribhanga pose, highlighting the artistic skill of Harappan craftsmen. Additional Information: Carnelian, a red semiprecious stone, was commonly used in Harappan beadmaking. Harappans exported carnelian, lapis lazuli, copper, gold, and various woods to Mesopotamia. The Harappan people produced a large number of terracotta figurines (made of fire-baked clay). The most important terracotta figurines among the Indus figures are those representing the mother goddess. Indus Valley people used gold for ornaments such as rings, amulets, and pendants.

s: The famous female figurine known as 'Dancing Girl', found at Mohenjo-daro, is made of
x: The world-famous female figurine found at Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilization, is known as the “Dancing Girl.” It is an approximately 10.5-centimetrehigh metal figurine, castusing the lost-wax technique. Its metallurgical analysis and archaeological descriptions indicate that it is made of bronze.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Harappan Culture is not correct ?
o: It witnessed the first cities in the subcontinent.
It marks the first use of script, written from right to left.
It marks the earliest known use of iron as a medium for the art of sculpting.
It marks the earliest known use of stone as a medium for the art of sculpting.
x: Harappan sculptures were made of bronze (lost-wax), steatite and red sandstone, so stone and metal were used, but iron was not used for sculpting; Harappan culture was a Bronze Age culture. Hence the iron statement is incorrect.
